detailed_description: The Chmod Calculator converts between octal and symbolic Unix file permission notation in the browser. You can toggle nine read, write, and execute checkboxes for owner, group, and other to update the three-digit octal value, or type an octal value directly to update the checkboxes. The page also shows the symbolic representation in `-rwxr-xr--` style and a `chmod <octal> filename` example, with a copy button for the chmod command. The tool does not parse symbolic strings such as `u=rwx,g=rx,o=r`, handle setuid, setgid, or sticky bits, work with extended ACLs, validate filesystem support, or apply changes to actual files.
usage_steps: Toggle the read, write, and execute checkboxes for owner, group, and other to set permissions.
Watch the three-digit octal value update as you change the checkboxes.
Or type a three-digit octal value such as 644 directly to set all the checkboxes at once.
Review the symbolic representation shown in `-rwxr-xr--` style.
Copy the generated `chmod <octal> filename` command from the output area.
usage_examples: Confirm that 644 maps to owner read/write and group/other read only.
Set the execute checkbox for the owner and confirm the octal value updates to 744.
Type 750 to see how the checkboxes for group execute and owner write line up.
Copy a `chmod 600 filename` command for a quick note before running it manually.
